newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks plunge on shaky politics.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks plunge on shaky politics.

text.p: Indian shares plunged on Monday, with the Bombay stock exchange's top 30 index closing more than three percent lower as investors ran scared from a market beset by political worries and a shaky economy, analysts said.
The Bombay index provisionally closed 3.19 percent lower than Friday, 98.86 points down at 3,002.41 after being 5.2 percent down at the height of the bear stampede.

There are worries that Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government could fall if the Congress Party carries out threats to quit the 13-party coalition to support its former leader, P.V. Narasimha Rao, in his fight against three corruption cases.
"Markets don't like any form of instability and worst of them is the political instability," said Ramdeo Agarwal, research head at brokerage firm Motilal S Oswal.
"I think the political crisis is surely there. Also, recession is staring it in the face. It is becoming scary," he said.
State Bank of India shares led the fall in blue chips after the central bank imposed a 24 percent cap on foreign holdings in the stock. SBI shares fell 11.25 rupees to close at 217.25 rupees.
Agarwal said the market was on course to settle around the index's 52-week low at 2,820.26. It closed just 183 points above that level on Monday.
Traders said foreign fund selling in blue-chip stocks sent the market reeling with no buyers to stem the fall.
Bajaj Auto, Hindalco, Indian Hotels, Grasim and ITC figured among the front-bench stocks that bore the selling brunt.
Other frontline stocks such as Reliance, Tisco and Telco bucked the trend in the early part of the session but suffered losses in late afternoon deals.
"Speculators are the front-runners in the market free fall. There is a near panic," said a chief trader at a foreign brokerage firm who did not wish to be identified.
"Foreign funds are sellers in many pivotals. The market is in a free fall with emergence of no buyers even at these lower levels," said another dealer.
